origins.section: 3.3.1 Spot the Problem: A Pool of Channels
3.6 A TLS Channel Checks the Host Only When You Tell It To
3.2 One Read Is Not One Message

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool: 3.3 says that when the timeout fires the 2.1.7 channel closes its socket before throwing, and that an answer sent later 'went into a connection that no longer existed'; 3.3.1 adds that for purchase 802 'the host's approval for it is lost'.
recorded.prompt:q-timeout-attribute: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-timeout-attribute: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-timeout-attribute: 3.5.1 says 'The timeout attribute is ignored. The channel reads only the timeout property and falls back to its default of five minutes', and its trace shows 300000 ms.
recorded.prompt:q-tls-machine-on-the-path: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tls-machine-on-the-path: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tls-machine-on-the-path: 3.6 says 'With serverauth false, which is the default, the 2.1.7 factory accepts any certificate', and that anyone in between can play the host; the trace row with serverauth=false and an untrusted cert shows messages flowing.
recorded.prompt:q-binary-keep-alive: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-binary-keep-alive: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-binary-keep-alive: 3.2 shows NACChannel with expect-keep-alive=false throwing ISOException 'receive length 0 seems strange' and says a ChannelAdaptor drops the connection on it. 3.5 says the adaptor reconnects after reconnect-delay (inference: 3.5 lists 'EOF, a read timeout or an unpack error' as triggers, and this length error falls under the 3.2 drop statement rather than being named there).

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:a: 3.3 and 3.3.1 say the channel closes on timeout and the next borrower gets a dead channel ('unconnected ISOChannel'), so there is no connection for the answer to wait in.
recorded.prompt:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:c: 3.3 says 'When the timeout fires it throws SocketTimeoutException', and the trace shows receive() throwing at 1044 ms with a 1000 ms timeout.
recorded.prompt:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-slow-answer-in-a-pool:d: The 3.3 trace shows 'host: sent the answer' at 1401 ms, after the client timed out. That shows the host still sends it (a short inference that the timeout is local to the client).
recorded.prompt:q-timeout-attribute:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-timeout-attribute:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-timeout-attribute:a: 3.5.1 says the channel reads only the timeout property, and 3.4 says the channel reads the <property> children.
recorded.prompt:q-timeout-attribute:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-timeout-attribute:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-timeout-attribute:b: 3.4 says 'Q2 gives its <property> children to both', and 3.5.1 says the attribute is ignored, so Q2 does not copy attributes.
recorded.prompt:q-timeout-attribute:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-timeout-attribute:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-timeout-attribute:d: 3.5.1 says the attribute is ignored, so it is never read. 3.8 lists the timeout property as a read timeout in ms with 0 disabling it, so there is no floor at the default (short inference).
recorded.prompt:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:b: 3.6 says trust in the keystore applies only 'With serverauth=true'; with the default false, any certificate is accepted.
recorded.prompt:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:c: 3.6 brings in the CN comparison as the step after enabling serverauth ('The factory then compares servername...'), and the serverauth=false row succeeds. That it happens only under serverauth=true is a short inference from 'then' plus 'accepts any certificate'.
recorded.prompt:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-tls-machine-on-the-path:d: 3.6 says the factory with serverauth false accepts 'any certificate', and an untrusted cert connects in the trace. The page never mentions the JDK trust store, but 'any certificate' covers a self-signed one.
recorded.prompt:q-binary-keep-alive:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-binary-keep-alive:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-binary-keep-alive:a: 3.2 says NACChannel and PostChannel accept a zero-length frame 'only with the property expect-keep-alive' and shows the error without it; only ASCIIChannel writes 0000 back and reads on.
recorded.prompt:q-binary-keep-alive:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-binary-keep-alive:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-binary-keep-alive:b: 3.4 says the Receiver 'calls receive() in a loop', and 3.2 says the adaptor drops the connection on the keep-alive. So the adaptor does not answer frames before the channel reads them (short inference).
recorded.prompt:q-binary-keep-alive:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-binary-keep-alive:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-binary-keep-alive:c: 3.5 shows the adaptor reconnecting by itself after reconnect-delay, and 3.7 says 'The adaptor reconnects by itself'.
